title: Increase the istiod gRPC receive limit for large ambient meshes

detection.reason: Affectedness depends on the aggregate number and serialized names and versions of ambient workloads and services, the istiod receive-limit configuration, and runtime logs; no single supported inventory field settles it.

quote: **WDS reconnect requests are larger in big ambient meshes** — On reconnect, ztunnel reports the name and version of every workload (WDS) resource it holds. This request can exceed istiod's default 4MiB gRPC receive limit, leaving ztunnel in a reconnect loop with `ResourceExhausted: grpc: received message larger than max` errors. Meshes could already hit the limit at roughly 55,000 workloads, since resource names were reported before this change; the added versions grow the request by about a third, lowering the trigger point to roughly 40,000 workloads (sooner with long resource names or many services). If your mesh is near this scale, raise `ISTIO_GPRC_MAXRECVMSGSIZE` on istiod — budget roughly 1MiB per 10,000 workloads and services; for example, `--set pilot.env.ISTIO_GPRC_MAXRECVMSGSIZE=33554432` (32MiB) covers meshes well past 300,000 resources — and watch istiod logs for the error above after upgrading.
remediation: If the mesh is near roughly 40,000 workloads, raise `ISTIO_GPRC_MAXRECVMSGSIZE` on istiod, budgeting roughly 1MiB per 10,000 workloads and services. Watch istiod logs for `ResourceExhausted: grpc: received message larger than max` after upgrading.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq '.items | length' # what output means: this is a rough pod-count indicator; meshes near the stated workload scale need the istiod limit and logs reviewed manually

title: Remove the removed gateway tracing feature flag

detection.reason: The setting is a control-plane environment variable and no supported inventory predicate determines whether it is configured or whether its value is false.

quote: **PILOT_SPAWN_UPSTREAM_SPAN_FOR_GATEWAY feature flag removed** — The environment variable `PILOT_SPAWN_UPSTREAM_SPAN_FOR_GATEWAY` has been removed. The behavior it controlled (spawning a separate tracing span for each upstream request for gateway when using the Telemetry API) is now always enabled. Users who explicitly set this variable to `false` to opt out of this behavior should be aware that the opt-out is no longer available.
remediation: Remove `PILOT_SPAWN_UPSTREAM_SPAN_FOR_GATEWAY` from the istiod configuration. Be aware that the opt-out is no longer available and the behavior is always enabled.
verifyCommand: kubectl get deployments -A -o yaml | grep -n -C 2 'PILOT_SPAWN_UPSTREAM_SPAN_FOR_GATEWAY' # what output means: matching istiod deployment configuration means the removed variable must be removed or reviewed

title: Review unhealthy endpoint sending behavior

detection.reason: The relevant OutlierDetection.minHealthPercent configuration and PILOT_AUTO_SEND_UNHEALTHY_ENDPOINTS environment variable are not represented by a single supported cluster-inventory field.

quote: **Default behavior for sending unhealthy endpoints** — By default, Istio will now send unhealthy endpoints unless `OutlierDetection.minHealthPercent` is being configured on a Service. This can be disabled by setting `PILOT_AUTO_SEND_UNHEALTHY_ENDPOINTS` to `false` or using compatibility profiles.
remediation: Review whether `OutlierDetection.minHealthPercent` is configured on a Service. If unhealthy endpoints should not be sent, set `PILOT_AUTO_SEND_UNHEALTHY_ENDPOINTS` to `false` or use compatibility profiles.
verifyCommand: kubectl get services,destinationrules -A -o yaml | grep -n -C 2 'minHealthPercent' # what output means: matching configuration should be reviewed; no match does not rule out other configuration sources

title: Re-register or label existing auto-registered WorkloadEntries
quote: **Existing auto-registered WorkloadEntries need re-registration or a manual label for HBONE** — The HBONE tunnel label is applied only when a WorkloadEntry is auto-created, so workloads auto-registered before upgrading continue to be reached over plaintext until either they re-register (reconnect a fresh instance) or the label (`networking.istio.io/tunnel=http`) is added to their existing WorkloadEntry.
remediation: Have workloads auto-registered before upgrading re-register by reconnecting a fresh instance, or add the label `networking.istio.io/tunnel=http` to their existing WorkloadEntry.
verifyCommand: kubectl get workloadentries -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.labels["networking.istio.io/tunnel"] == "http") | [.metadata.namespace,.metadata.name] | @tsv' # what output means: listed WorkloadEntries have the HBONE label; existing auto-registered entries not listed need re-registration or the label

title: Review custom MCP consumers of the XDS API generator

detection.reason: Custom MCP consumers and their connection behavior are not represented by a supported cluster-inventory predicate; determining whether they connect from non-system namespaces requires manual review.

quote: **The XDS api generator now requires a control-plane identity** — Custom MCP consumers connecting to istiod's api generator from non-system namespaces are now rejected. Standard sidecar, gateway, and ztunnel traffic is unaffected. To restore previous behavior, set ENABLE_XDS_API_GENERATOR_AUTH=false.
remediation: Review custom MCP consumers connecting to istiod's api generator from non-system namespaces. To restore previous behavior, set `ENABLE_XDS_API_GENERATOR_AUTH=false`.
verifyCommand: kubectl get pods -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | [.metadata.namespace,.metadata.name,([.spec.containers[].image] | join(" "))] | @tsv' | grep -i 'mcp' # what output means: matching pods are candidates for manual review as custom MCP consumers
